title: Suspension and Discharge of a Workers' Compensation Referral
content:
# Suspension and discharge

## When treatment is suspended

Treatment under a Workers' Compensation Referral is suspended:

- when the authorization lapses;
- when the claim is denied;
- when the pending-claim visit allowance is used; or
- when the consecutive missed visits on the referral reach the program's consecutive-missed-visit figure for an adjuster review (non-compliance review).

Consecutive missed visits are the missed visits reported on this referral since its latest recorded visit, or since the referral was opened where none is recorded.

Treatment resumes when the reason is resolved.

## Discharge from suspension

A suspended referral is discharged no earlier than the program's longest suspension in calendar days after the suspension start date on file. Days are counted as calendar days from the suspension start date, the suspension start date itself being day zero.

- **The clock starts** on the suspension start date recorded on the referral.
- **Boundary** — discharge may occur on the day the count equals the program's longest suspension, or later; it may not occur earlier.

### Boundary cases (hypothetical, for a 14-day longest suspension)

| Day of the count | May the suspended referral be discharged? |
|---|---|
| day 13 | No |
| day 14 | Yes — the boundary day qualifies |
| day 20 | Yes |

## Discharge at the end of the program

A program that reaches the program's maximum length in weeks from its first date of service is discharged.

## Consecutive missed visits (hypothetical)

In a program whose figure for an adjuster review is 2: a visit is recorded on a Monday, then a no-show on Wednesday and a late cancellation on Friday are reported. Two missed visits have been reported since the latest recorded visit, which reaches the figure, and treatment is suspended for a non-compliance review.
